accordionDocs.descriptionBody1: An accordion is a versatile user interface element designed to enhance user experience within digital interfaces. They are commonly employed in various contexts, such as FAQ sections, product descriptions, or content-heavy web pages.
accordionDocs.descriptionBody2: Accordions provide users with the ability to selectively expand and collapse sections, improving content accessibility and streamlining navigation. This versatile component is a valuable addition to any design system, empowering creators to craft user-friendly interfaces while maintaining a cohesive design language.
accordionDocs.featuresBody: Here's what you need to know about the noteworthy features of Accordion component.
accordionDocs.feature1Body: Effortlessly create nested accordion sections without the need for manual assembly, simplifying complex layouts.
accordionDocs.feature2Body: Choose from various positions for the expand/collapse icon, on the left or right.
accordionDocs.feature3Body: Edit the accordion text without the need to double-click, making the user experience smoother.
accordionDocs.sectionBody: Allows you to display content in a collapsible manner, making it easy for users to access information while conserving screen space.
accordionDocs.examplesBody: Here you can find various examples for Accordion for best practices and inspiration.
accordionDocs.faqAccount: How do I update my account information?
accordionDocs.faqAccountAnswer: Go to Settings, then Profile, edit the fields you need and save your changes.
accordionDocs.faqPaymentAnswer: Major credit and debit cards like Visa, MasterCard, and American Express, as well as digital payment options like PayPal and Apple Pay.
accordionDocs.faqTrack: How can I track my order?
accordionDocs.faqTrackAnswer: Open Orders in your account and select the order to see its live delivery status.
accordionDocs.faqPassword: How do I reset my password?
accordionDocs.faqPasswordAnswer: On the sign-in page choose “Forgot password” and follow the link we email you.

badgeDocs.descriptionBody2: Whether you need to highlight a new feature, emphasize important information, or signify different user statuses, our badges provide the perfect solution to add clarity and visual appeal to your designs.
badgeDocs.featuresBody: Here's what you need to know about the noteworthy features of Badge component.
badgeDocs.feature1Body: Explore a wide selection of 9 distinct colors to match your design's color scheme.
badgeDocs.feature2Body: Choose from 3 distinct styles to tailor your badges to your design aesthetics.
badgeDocs.feature3Body: Utilize Number & Status badges to signify notifications or convey statuses such as success, error, and more.
badgeDocs.sectionBadgeBody: Enables you to visually highlight or display additional information within limited screen space.

buttonGroupDocs.descriptionBody1: Button Groups, a vital component within our design system, offer a seamless way to organize and present multiple buttons or actions cohesively. These groups are particularly useful in user interfaces where various actions need to be presented together for clarity and efficiency.

avatarDocs.descriptionBody1: Avatars within a design system serve as visual representations of users or entities, frequently employed as profile images or placeholders. avatarDocs.descriptionBody2: Our avatars offer an array of features, including variations in style, such as memoji and illustrations, top and bottom status indicators, avatar groups, and more. These features enhance the personalization and versatility of our avatar collection, ensuring they seamlessly integrate into your design projects.

datePickerDocs.descriptionBody1: The Date Picker component is a crucial element within our design system, serving as a fundamental tool for users to select dates. Also, we recognize the importance of providing a comprehensive solution for date-related interactions, which is why we have included not only the Date Picker but also the Range Picker, filters, and various other features, ensuring that our design system covers a wide range of date selection and filtering needs for your projects.

datePickerDocs.feature1Body: Offers versatile date selection options. With the regular Date Picker, you can easily pick single dates and the Range Picker allows you to select date ranges efficiently, making it ideal for a variety of date-related tasks.
datePickerDocs.feature2Body: The Date Picker component is enhanced with Time Filter and Footer options, making it even more functional. They enable precise date-time filtering and provide additional information and interactive elements below.
datePickerDocs.feature3Body: Day Cells offer numerous states and options, allowing you to create a date picker that aligns perfectly with your design vision. From highlighting special dates to adjusting the appearance of each day cell, you have the flexibility.

ratingDocs.descriptionBody1: Ratings let users express or view an opinion at a glance, using stars, hearts, numbers or emojis. In our design system, we've built them to work standalone, inside a review summary, or as an interactive bar for collecting feedback.
ratingDocs.descriptionBody2: Whether you need a quick star average on a product card or a full Rating Bar for a post-purchase survey, these components adapt to the context.
ratingDocs.featuresBody: Here's what you need to know about the noteworthy features of Ratings component.
ratingDocs.feature1Body: Star and heart glyphs with empty, half and filled states, the building blocks of every rating display.
ratingDocs.feature2Body: Combine a rating with a value, a count, and a link button to show a full review summary.
ratingDocs.feature3Body: Collect feedback with an interactive bar of emojis, numbers, stars or hearts.

sliderDocs.descriptionBody1: Sliders let users pick a precise value, or a range of values, by dragging a thumb along a track. In our design system they carry an optional label and a live value readout.
sliderDocs.descriptionBody2: A Range Slider is the same control with two thumbs, for picking a minimum and a maximum within a single span.
sliderDocs.featuresBody: Here's what you need to know about the noteworthy features of Slider component.
sliderDocs.feature1Body: Drag a single thumb along a track to select a value within a specified range.
sliderDocs.feature2Body: Use two thumbs to define both a minimum and a maximum value within a specified range.
sliderDocs.feature3Body: An optional label and a live value readout keep the current selection clear at a glance.
sliderDocs.sectionSliderBody: Allowing precise selection of a single value within a specified range.
sliderDocs.sectionRangeBody: Empowers users to define both minimum and maximum values within a specified range, with the option to display the selected span.

switchDocs.descriptionBody1: Switch and Toggle both let users move between choices, but for different jobs: a Switch flips a single setting on or off, while a Toggle Item picks one option from a short segmented list.
switchDocs.descriptionBody2: We've built both with clear label placement and full keyboard support, so they fit settings panels, toolbars, and everything between discrete choices.
switchDocs.featuresBody: Here's what you need to know about the noteworthy features of Switch Toggle component.
switchDocs.feature1Body: A single on/off control with a clear label, for settings that are either enabled or disabled.
switchDocs.feature2Body: A segmented row of options, for switching between a small set of discrete choices.
switchDocs.feature3Body: Both controls accept an icon beside the label, for quicker scanning.

stepDocs.descriptionBody1: Step Indicators show users where they are in a multi-step process — a checkout, an onboarding flow, a wizard — and how many steps remain. In our design system, they come in horizontal and vertical orientations.
stepDocs.descriptionBody2: Each step carries a number, a label, and a state — upcoming, current, or completed — so users always know what's next.
stepDocs.featuresBody: Here's what you need to know about the noteworthy features of Step Indicator component.
stepDocs.feature1Body: Choose the orientation that fits your layout — a horizontal row for a checkout, or a vertical list for a sidebar.
stepDocs.feature2Body: Numbered, current, and completed states are visually distinct, so users always know their progress.
stepDocs.feature3Body: Customize labels, connectors, and states to match the flow you're building.

textInputDocsOv.sectionTextInputBody: A versatile tool for capturing and displaying textual data within your application, available in a variety of input types.
textInputDocsOv.descriptionBody1: The Text Input is the workhorse of any form: a versatile tool for capturing and displaying textual data, available in a variety of input types.
textInputDocsOv.descriptionBody2: Each type is a preset rather than a paint job — it carries the keyboard a phone will show, the autofill bucket the browser will use, and whether the value stays Latin in a Persian UI.
textInputDocsOv.spotlight5: Label, hint and error built in
textInputDocsOv.featuresBody: Here's what you need to know about the noteworthy features of the Text Input component.
textInputDocsOv.feature1Body: Email, password, card, website, amount, search, emoji and more — each with the right keyboard and autofill behaviour.
textInputDocsOv.feature2Body: Leading and trailing slots take icons, attached blocks or controls, so an icon on one side and a unit on the other is expressible.
textInputDocsOv.feature3Body: Label, hint and error ship with the input, so htmlFor, aria-describedby, aria-invalid and role="alert" are never the thing an app forgets.
textInputDocsOv.sectionStatesBody: Default, filled, hover, focus, disabled and error, across the three sizes.
textInputDocsOv.sectionTagBody: A specialized input component designed for creating and managing tags.
textInputDocsOv.sectionCounterBody: A numeric field with increment and decrement controls attached to it.
textInputDocsOv.sectionDigitBody: A component designed for capturing numeric data one digit at a time — one-time codes and PINs.
textInputDocsOv.sectionInlineBody: A compact input for capturing data directly within content, switching between reading and editing in place.

typographyDocs.descriptionBody1: Typography is the art and science of arranging text in a visually pleasing and communicative manner, forming an essential foundation within a design system. It defines how text appears across elements, ensuring a consistent and coherent visual identity.
typographyDocs.descriptionBody2: Nili sets Latin in Inter and Inter Display and Persian in Vazirmatn. Both are variable and both are subsetted by unicode-range, so an English page never downloads the Arabic cut.
typographyDocs.featuresBody: Here's what you need to know about the noteworthy features of the Typography element.
typographyDocs.feature1Body: Titles and Labels use Inter Display, the large optical size; everything else uses Inter. Persian swaps both to Vazirmatn.
typographyDocs.feature2Body: Line heights and tracking come straight from the design file, so text on screen matches the frame rather than approximating it.
typographyDocs.feature3Body: The same numbers exist as Tailwind classes and as data, so tokens, docs and components can never drift apart.
typographyDocs.pangram: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.
typographyDocs.sectionTableBody: The same numbers, in the shape you want when picking a variant rather than admiring one.

countryFlagDocs.descriptionBody1: Country flags are visual representations of nations, each with its own colours, patterns and symbolism. In a design system they help users identify and connect with countries, languages or regions.
countryFlagDocs.descriptionBody2: Whether it is a language preference, a regional setting or a phone prefix, a flag is a fast and unambiguous way to say which place is meant.
countryFlagDocs.featuresBody: Here's what you need to know about the noteworthy features of the Country Flag assets.
countryFlagDocs.feature1Body: Every ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country, a long tail of subdivisions, and a handful of non-country flags.
countryFlagDocs.feature2Body: The same 20px circle the Dropdown, Text Input and Tag components expect in their leading slot.
countryFlagDocs.feature3Body: Each flag is a cached static file, so a 250-row picker costs no JavaScript and loads only what scrolls into view.
countryFlagDocs.sectionSubdivisionsBody: States, provinces and constituent countries, under codes like gb-eng and us-hi.
countryFlagDocs.sectionOtherBody: Non-country flags: chequered, UN, and a few more.
countryFlagDocs.sectionSizesBody: Six named sizes, and a hairline for flags with a white edge.
countryFlagDocs.sectionFinderBody: Search the whole set by code or English name.

placeholderLogoDocs.descriptionBody1: Placeholder logos are temporary visual stand-ins, so designers and developers can map out the visual landscape of a project without borrowing anyone's brand.
placeholderLogoDocs.descriptionBody2: Nine fictional companies, each with a mark, a colour, an industry and plausible details. None of them exist, which is the point: a screenshot with one in it needs nobody's permission.
placeholderLogoDocs.featuresBody: Here's what you need to know about the noteworthy features of the Placeholder Logo assets.
placeholderLogoDocs.feature1Body: Finance, healthcare, energy, education, e-commerce and more, so a mock list reads as a real one.
placeholderLogoDocs.feature2Body: Nine distinct marks on nine distinct colours, drawn for this repo rather than sourced.
placeholderLogoDocs.feature3Body: Nothing here is anyone's trademark, so these can ship in marketing material without a clearance step.
placeholderLogoDocs.sectionLogosBody: Nine logos plus an empty-state variant, each in three versions.
placeholderLogoDocs.sectionDetailsBody: The fictional company behind each mark — industry, location, size and contact.

dropdownItemDocs.descriptionBody1: The Dropdown Item offers interactive options, information or actions that users can engage with inside a Dropdown, a command palette or a context menu.
dropdownItemDocs.descriptionBody2: Items take a leading visual — an icon, a flag, an avatar, a card mark or a company logo — and an optional second line, so one component covers every list the system draws.
dropdownItemDocs.featuresBody: Here's what you need to know about the noteworthy features of the Dropdown Item component.
dropdownItemDocs.feature1Body: The item is one component; whatever sits on its leading edge is data.
dropdownItemDocs.feature2Body: Add checkboxes, avatars, badges, shortcuts and descriptions without a new variant.
dropdownItemDocs.feature3Body: Leading and trailing slots both take arbitrary content, and labels are yours to write.
dropdownItemDocs.sectionItemBody: Offering interactive options, information or actions that users can engage with.
dropdownItemDocs.sectionMiscBody: Search, buttons and footer notes that live alongside the options rather than among them.
